events.title: Rooftop solar boom peaks
events.text: Over 10,000 Utah homes added rooftop solar in one year. The state had some of the fastest residential solar growth in America.

events.title: Hydrogen storage hub announced
events.text: Mitsubishi and Magnum announced the Advanced Clean Energy Storage project: underground salt caverns near Delta to hold green hydrogen made from renewables.

events.title: IPP goes from coal to gas
events.text: Los Angeles stopped taking coal power from Intermountain. The plant opened new gas turbines designed to burn up to 30% green hydrogen, climbing to 100% by 2045.

signature_plant.name: Intermountain Power Project
signature_plant.fact: For nearly 40 years this single Utah plant kept Los Angeles' lights on through a high-voltage line that crosses three states.

VT.summary: Vermont has the cleanest electricity in the country, with almost no fossil fuels. For 40 years one nuclear plant, Vermont Yankee, supplied most of the in-state power. After it closed in 2014, the state leaned harder on hydro from Quebec, plus its own dams, biomass, and a growing fleet of wind and solar.

events.title: Great Flood spurs new dams
events.text: A devastating November 1927 flood killed dozens and washed out many small power dams. Rebuilding led to a wave of new hydro stations that still run today.

events.title: Vermont Yankee reactor opens
events.text: A nuclear plant in Vernon began running. For decades it made most of the electricity used in Vermont.

events.title: Big Hydro-Quebec contract signed
events.text: Vermont utilities signed a 26-year deal to buy huge amounts of clean hydropower from Canada. It now covers nearly a third of the state's electricity.

events.title: Kingdom Community Wind opens
events.text: A 63 MW wind farm on a ridge in Lowell came online. It was the biggest power plant built in Vermont in decades and is still the state's largest today.

events.title: Vermont Yankee shuts down
events.text: Cheap fracked gas had made the old reactor unprofitable. Entergy closed it on December 29. Vermont's grid became almost entirely renewable.

events.title: 100% clean electricity law
events.text: Vermont passed a law requiring 100% renewable electricity by 2035. It cemented the state's spot as #1 cleanest grid in America.

signature_plant.name: Kingdom Community Wind
signature_plant.fact: Its 21 turbines sit on a ridge in Lowell that is so windy that locals say the trees grow sideways.

VA.summary: Virginia's grid was reshaped by two things: nuclear power and data centers. Dominion built four reactors at Surry and North Anna in the 1970s. Then in the 2010s, northern Virginia became the data center capital of the world. AI is now driving electricity demand through the roof, and Dominion is racing to build new gas plants and even small modular reactors to keep up.

events.title: Surry nuclear plant opens
events.text: Dominion's Surry Power Station, on the James River across from Jamestown, started its first reactor in December. It was Virginia's first nuclear plant.

events.title: North Anna goes online
events.text: Dominion's bigger nuclear plant on Lake Anna started running. Its two reactors still make more power than any other plant in the state.

events.title: MAE-East kicks off Data Center Alley
events.text: One of the world's first major internet exchange points opened in Tysons Corner. Loudoun County's quiet farmland slowly became the center of global internet traffic.

events.title: Virginia Clean Economy Act
events.text: A new law required Dominion to retire fossil fuel plants and go 100% clean by 2045, with Appalachian Power on a 2050 deadline. It also pushed offshore wind.

events.title: Data centers drive 24% of demand
events.text: Data centers now use almost a quarter of all Dominion's Virginia electricity. The utility says it needs $50 billion in new lines and plants by 2029 to keep up.

events.title: Dominion proposes 14% rate hike
events.text: To pay for the data center build-out, Dominion asked regulators to raise residential bills by 14%. Homeowners are pushing back hard.

signature_plant.name: North Anna Nuclear Generating Station
signature_plant.fact: The plant's cooling pond, Lake Anna, is so big it has become a popular vacation spot, with one warmer 'hot side' kept toasty by reactor heat year-round.

WI.summary: Wisconsin's grid has been a coal-and-nuclear mix for decades. Two reactors at Point Beach on Lake Michigan still run, and the state's last new big coal plant, Elm Road, came online in 2010 and 2011. Now WEC Energy is racing to retire those coal units and convert the rest to natural gas, while solar farms quickly fill in the gaps.

events.title: Point Beach nuclear comes online
events.text: Wisconsin Electric started its first reactor at Point Beach, on the shores of Lake Michigan. A second unit followed in 1972.

events.title: Elm Road coal units go online
events.text: Two big new coal units at the Oak Creek site started running. At over 1,200 MW combined, Elm Road was one of the last major US coal plants ever built.

events.title: Kewaunee nuclear plant shuts
events.text: Dominion closed the Kewaunee reactor on May 7, blaming cheap fracked gas. Wisconsin lost about 20% of its zero-carbon electricity overnight.

events.title: WEC accelerates coal exit
events.text: WEC Energy moved up plans to stop burning coal. Elm Road will be converted to natural gas, ending Wisconsin's long reliance on coal.

events.title: Point Beach licensed to age 80
events.text: Federal regulators cleared Point Beach to run until the early 2050s. Wisconsin's only remaining nuclear plant will keep providing carbon-free power for decades.

signature_plant.name: Elm Road Generating Station
signature_plant.fact: Built as one of America's last new coal plants in 2010, Elm Road is already being converted to burn natural gas instead, less than 20 years later.

WY.summary: Wyoming digs up about 40% of all the coal in America, mostly from huge open-pit mines in the Powder River Basin. Most of that coal moves out of state by train, but the rest fuels Wyoming's own grid, which is still the most coal-heavy in the US. Strong winds and a brand new nuclear project are starting to change the picture.

events.title: Clean Air Act fuels coal boom
events.text: Tougher air rules pushed power plants to buy Wyoming's low-sulfur coal. Giant new strip mines opened across the Powder River Basin.

events.title: Wyoming becomes #1 in coal
events.text: Wyoming surpassed Kentucky and West Virginia to become America's top coal-producing state. It has held the crown ever since.

events.title: Jim Bridger plant fires up
events.text: PacifiCorp's huge Jim Bridger station, near Rock Springs, began running its first coal unit. It is still the largest power plant in Wyoming.

events.title: Wyoming wind tax remains
events.text: Wyoming is the only US state that taxes wind power generation. Developers still poured in because the wind here is some of the strongest in the country.

events.title: TerraPower breaks ground at Kemmerer
events.text: On April 23, Bill Gates' TerraPower officially started building America's first big advanced nuclear reactor in Kemmerer, replacing a retiring coal plant. The 345 MW Natrium reactor uses sodium to cool itself and is aimed for 2030.

events.title: TransWest line under construction
events.text: After 18 years of permits and lawsuits, the giant TransWest Express transmission line broke ground in Wyoming in June 2023 to carry Wyoming wind 732 miles to Las Vegas.

signature_plant.name: Jim Bridger Power Plant
signature_plant.fact: Two of Jim Bridger's four big coal units were converted to run on natural gas in 2024, marking a slow shift even at the biggest plant in coal country.
